title: Systematic Evolution of Magnetic Anisotropy and Crystal-electric-field Ground States in SmTr2Ge2
authors: Ryuji Higashinaka, Kokoro Higo, Tatsuma D. Matsuda, Yuji Aoki
abstract: We investigated the crystal-electric-field (CEF) states in SmTr2Ge2 (Tr= Co-Cu and Ag) with the ThCr2Si2-type structure by magnetization and specific heat measurements. The magnetic anisotropy evolves systematically with Tr, changing from an easy ab plane for Tr = Co and Ni to an easy c axis for Tr = Cu and Ag. Combined analyses of the low-temperature susceptibility and magnetic entropy indicate a level crossing of the CEF ground state between Ni and Cu, together with a systematic evolution of the first excited CEF energy. The evolution of the magnetic properties correlates with changes in local structural parameters, providing an experimental basis for discussing how the ligand environment around the Sm ion is related to the 4f electronic state.
summary: This work experimentally investigates how the magnetic anisotropy and Crystal-Electric-Field (CEF) ground states evolve across the $	ext{SmTr}_2	ext{Ge}_2$ series by varying the transition metal $	ext{Tr}$. By measuring magnetization, specific heat, and susceptibility, the authors demonstrate a clear transition in magnetic behavior linked to the underlying CEF state and the local structural environment around the $	ext{Sm}$ ion.
main_problem: To systematically investigate the evolution of magnetic anisotropy and crystal-electric-field (CEF) ground states in the $	ext{SmTr}_2	ext{Ge}_2$ series.
main_result: The magnetic anisotropy systematically changes from easy $ab$ plane ($	ext{Co}, 	ext{Ni}$) to easy $c$ axis ($	ext{Cu}, 	ext{Ag}$), correlating with the evolution of the CEF ground state and local structural parameters.
method: Measurements include magnetization, specific heat, and magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$) as a function of temperature and applied field, complemented by structural analysis.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the $	ext{SmTr}_2	ext{Ge}_2$ compounds ($	ext{Tr} = 	ext{Co}, 	ext{Ni}, 	ext{Cu}, 	ext{Ag}$) with the $	ext{ThCr}_2	ext{Si}_2$-type structure, where magnetism originates from the $	ext{Sm}^{3+}$ $4f$ electrons.
key_observables: Magnetic anisotropy (easy plane vs. easy axis), CEF ground state evolution, magnetic entropy, and resistivity ($ho(T)$) changes below $T_N$.
important_parameters: Transition metal identity ($	ext{Tr}$), applied magnetic field ($H=1	ext{ T}$), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses $	ext{La}$ nonmagnetic analogs to isolate the $	ext{Sm}$ contribution to magnetic susceptibility and specific heat.

paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes magnetic measurements ($\chi, C_p, M$) across the $	ext{Tr}$ series, correlating the observed changes in magnetic anisotropy and CEF ground state with the local structural environment determined by X-ray measurements.
why_interesting: The systematic tuning of magnetic anisotropy via ligand environment (changing $	ext{Tr}$) provides a clear experimental platform to study how crystal fields dictate the low-energy magnetic excitations in $4f$ electron systems.
